llcFilesWith: Alabama Secretary of State (Application to Register or Renew Trademark, Service Mark or Trade Name, Form LAT-4)
soleProprietorFilesWith: Alabama Secretary of State as well, on the same trade name application; Alabama has no mandatory DBA filing, so registration is optional for any owner
feeBasis: Ala. Code § 8-12-8(d) sets a $30 filing fee for the application, and § 8-12-10(a) sets the same $30 for a renewal; the Secretary of State's fee schedule lists Trademark (Registration or Renewal) at $30.00 under both sections, and Form LAT-4 asks for the same amount. The registration runs five years. Filing through the state's online portal adds a portal surcharge that the state does not publish as a figure. Registration is voluntary; Alabama does not require a business to register a name it trades under.
renewalRule: Renewable for successive five-year terms; the renewal application must be filed within the six months before the registration expires and must state that the mark is still in use in Alabama. The Secretary of State writes to the registrant's last known address during the year before expiry to say a renewal is due.
protectionNote: Alabama is unusual in having no separate assumed-name or DBA statute; the only way to register a name you trade under is to register it as a trade name under the trademark chapter (Title 8, Chapter 12), where "trade name" is defined by § 8-12-6(10) as a name adopted and used to identify a business and distinguish it from the business of others. That registration is more than disclosure: § 8-12-16 gives the owner of a registered mark a civil action against anyone whose use is likely to cause confusion, with the remedies in § 8-12-18, so it functions like a state trademark rather than a bare notice filing. It sits in the trademark register, separate from the entity-name distinguishability records used at formation, and § 8-12-7(b) says a reserved or registered corporate name bestows no ownership rights in a mark.
searchNote: Registered trade names and marks are searched in the Secretary of State's Government Records Inquiry System, which offers three trademark entry points (mark description, applicant name, and trademark number) and is separate from the business-entity records. Because Alabama does not require DBA registration, an unregistered trade name in actual use will not appear in either search.
notes: Alabama has no mandatory DBA system. A business that wants to secure a name it trades under registers it as a trade name with the Secretary of State under the trademark chapter for $30, good for five years and renewable, and that registration carries trademark-style protection rather than mere disclosure. This is the reverse of most states, where DBA registration is required but confers no rights: in Alabama it is optional but does confer rights. The Secretary of State's own trademarks page makes the same point in the other direction, noting that rejection of a registration does not prevent use of the mark because ownership arises from common-law adoption and use. The current paper form is LAT-4, which covers both registration and renewal; the older registration-only LAT-1 is still on the server but is no longer linked from the trademarks page.
